feedback: Getting better, but feels slightly dragged out and less smooth. Closer, not yet approved.

request.instructions: Speak in clear Modern Standard Arabic as a warm, composed preschool teacher addressing a small class. Use a natural feminine speaking voice in a comfortable middle register, with a clear steady tone and small pitch variations. Sound attentive and gently encouraging, with understated expression. Speak each complete letter name as one smooth, continuous utterance at a natural conversational pace. Keep consonants clear and Arabic long vowels correct; release each sound naturally without extra holding, internal pauses or stretching the ending. Avoid breathiness, whispering, vocal fry and sing-song pitch glides. Read only each Arabic letter name written in the script, in order. Say each name once. Leave a clear two-second silent pause between names. No introduction, numbers, commentary, music or additional sounds.

constraints: No automatic retry or full batch.
Preserve earlier samples and approved game files.
Keep written Arabic, vowel-length distinctions, model, voice and speed unchanged.
No pitch shifting or time stretching.
Owner judges the audio; no acoustic verification requested.
expectation: Test smoother pacing without losing the composed tone; not a guaranteed match.
